name: The accounting equation
description: Assets = Liabilities + Equity, always. Every transaction keeps the equation in balance.

name: What each statement does
description: The balance sheet is a snapshot of position; the income statement and cash flow statement are films of performance and cash movement over a period.

name: Income statement anatomy
description: Revenue down to net income: gross profit, operating income, pretax income, and what belongs in each section.

name: Balance sheet anatomy
description: Current vs non-current assets and liabilities, and the components of equity.

name: Cash flow statement anatomy
description: Operating, investing, and financing sections, and which activities belong where.

name: Current vs non-current
description: The one-year (or operating-cycle) test that splits the balance sheet.

name: Debits and credits
description: Which accounts increase with a debit, which with a credit, and why the books always balance.

name: Reading journal entries
description: Given an entry, say what happened in the business; given an event, write the entry.

name: Accrual vs cash accounting
description: Revenue and expenses are recorded when earned and incurred, not when cash moves. The gap between the two is where analysis lives.

name: What counts as revenue
description: Revenue is earned by delivering goods or services, not by collecting cash or booking orders.

name: Expense recognition and matching
description: Costs follow the revenue they help produce; period costs hit when incurred.

name: Net income and where it goes
description: The bottom line, and the fact that it flows into retained earnings rather than sitting in cash.

name: Dividends
description: Distributions to owners reduce retained earnings; they are not an expense.

name: Retained earnings roll-forward
description: Opening RE + net income − dividends = closing RE. The hinge that links the income statement to the balance sheet.

name: Non-cash charges
description: Depreciation, amortization, and impairments reduce income without touching cash, so they are added back in CFO.

name: Working capital changes
description: A rise in receivables or inventory consumes cash; a rise in payables releases it. Balance sheet deltas explain CFO vs net income.

name: Derive CFO by the indirect method
description: Start from net income, add back non-cash charges, adjust for working capital deltas: cash from operations, rebuilt from the other two statements.

name: PP&E roll-forward
description: Opening PP&E + capex − depreciation − disposals = closing PP&E. Links the balance sheet to capex on the cash flow statement.

name: Equity roll-forward
description: Share issuance, buybacks, net income, dividends, and OCI reconcile opening to closing equity.

name: Cash ties out
description: CFO + CFI + CFF + FX effect equals the change in cash on the balance sheet. If it doesn't, something is wrong.

name: Why CFO differs from net income
description: Explaining the gap between earnings and operating cash for a specific company — the single most useful habit in statement reading.

name: Revenue recognition choices
description: Timing, gross vs net, percentage of completion, bill-and-hold: where management judgement enters the top line.

name: Deferred revenue
description: Cash collected before it is earned is a liability, and its movement is a signal about future revenue.

name: Inventory methods (FIFO/LIFO)
description: The cost-flow assumption changes COGS, margins, and inventory values when prices move.

name: LIFO reserve adjustment
description: Use the LIFO reserve to restate LIFO inventory and COGS to a FIFO basis for comparison.

name: Capitalize vs expense
description: Capitalizing a cost moves it from the income statement to the balance sheet today and spreads it over the future — a lever that can be abused.

name: Depreciation estimates
description: Useful life and salvage value are estimates; changing them changes earnings with no change in cash.

name: Leases
description: Right-of-use assets and lease liabilities put long-term rent commitments on the balance sheet.

name: Deferred taxes
description: Book-tax timing differences create deferred tax assets and liabilities.

name: Valuation allowance
description: A reserve against deferred tax assets that says management doubts future taxable income — a forward-looking tell.

name: Impairments and write-downs
description: Assets written down when carrying value exceeds recoverable value; goodwill impairments confess overpayment for acquisitions.

name: Share-based compensation
description: A real expense paid in shares: non-cash on the CFS, dilutive to owners.

name: Common-size statements
description: Everything as a percent of revenue or assets, making companies of different sizes comparable.

name: Liquidity ratios
description: Current and quick ratios: can the company cover near-term obligations.

name: Solvency and leverage ratios
description: Debt to equity, debt to EBITDA, and the capital structure's margin for error.

name: Coverage ratios
description: Interest coverage: how many times operating profit covers the interest bill.

name: Activity ratios and the cash cycle
description: DSO, DIO, DPO, and turnover: how fast the business converts work into cash.

name: Profitability ratios
description: Margins and returns on assets and equity.

name: DuPont decomposition
description: ROE split into margin × turnover × leverage: which engine drives the returns, and which is fragile.

name: Trend analysis
description: Multi-year direction beats single-year level. What is improving, what is deteriorating, and is the story consistent.

name: Industry fingerprints
description: A grocer, a software company, an airline, and a bank have unmistakable statement shapes. Learn to read the silhouette.

name: Accruals and earnings quality
description: Earnings backed by cash are worth more than earnings built from accruals. Large or growing accruals predict reversals.

name: DSO and DIO drift
description: Receivables or inventory growing faster than sales is the most common early warning in financial statements.

name: Channel stuffing and pull-forwards
description: Pushing product to distributors or booking tomorrow's sales today: revenue up, DSO up, cash flat, and a cliff next quarter.

name: Cookie-jar reserves
description: Over-reserving in good times and releasing reserves in bad times smooths earnings and hides deterioration.

name: Improper capitalization
description: Operating costs parked on the balance sheet inflate current earnings — WorldCom's playbook.

name: Assembling a forensic case
description: One odd number is noise; three that point the same way are a thesis. Name the technique and cite the evidence.

name: Knowing where things live
description: Which note answers which question: revenue, debt, leases, taxes, contingencies, related parties.

name: Asking the right question
description: Specific, evidence-anchored questions that a CFO cannot deflect without revealing something.
